> 升。元亨，用見大人，勿恤，南征吉。

Hexagram 46 is about rising, and its character is not a climbing figure at all — it is a measuring scoop.

## 升 is a pictograph of a measure

升 is a pictograph: a ladle-shaped grain measure with a handle. 說文: 升，十龠也 — ten 龠 to a 合, ten 合 to a 升.

So the original sense is "a measure," not "to ascend."

And the 易 uses it for ascent with exactly the action of that measure in mind: rising one grade at a time, graduated, in order — not one leap.

Which makes the whole chapter: 升 is measured upward. It is not flown upward.

## 允升

初六 允升，大吉.

允: trustworthy, fitting. 說文 允，信也.

Read together: rising as one who can be trusted — a foundation that is real, and then it is fit to go up.

The first line is at the very bottom, corresponding to the fourth; it has no other capital, only 允.

## 禴: two hexagrams, one thin offering

九二 孚乃利用禴，無咎.

禴 is the summer offering, the thinnest of the four: new vegetables, no animal.

And 萃六二 uses the same word in the same phrase. Two hexagrams, both saying: thin offering, and sincerity.

## 升虛邑

九三 升虛邑.

虛: empty. 邑: a walled town.

Rising into an empty town — and the reading has to hold: 虛邑 is not a rich place, it is a place with nobody in it.

So the line is not simply "favourable." It is favourable to the point that there is no resistance. Which is why the book marks it: 顺得过了头 — the ease has gone past what is healthy.

## 王用亨于岐山

六四: the king presents at Mount Qi.

亨 is 享, to offer. 岐山 is the Zhou holy ground — the Zhou moved from Bin to the foot of Qi, and the dynastic enterprise began there.

(王 is usually read as King Wen, sometimes Wu; this book keeps both and decides neither.)

## 升階

六五 貞吉，升階.

階: the steps.

拾級而上 — step by step, in clear order.

And the measure of the line is in that one character: steps are made for feet, not for jumping. Jump one, and the foot lands on nothing.

## 冥升

上六 冥升，利於不息之貞.

冥: dark, dim. 說文 冥，幽也.

冥升 — rising in the dark. This is the easiest line in the chapter to read backwards: it is not "quietly cultivating oneself." It is "going up while unable to see."

The evidence is in the 象: 冥升在上，消不富也 — 消 is depletion, 不富 is not increasing.

At the very top, going further only depletes. And the reason it is still 利於不息之貞 is that in such a position the one thing still available is to keep holding correct without stopping.

## 順德，積小以高大

The 象: 君子以順德，積小以高大.

順 is not compliance — it is following a thing's own nature. 德 is its substance.

So: follow the grain of what it is, and thicken its substance a little at a time.

Which is the exact opposite of force: force bends a thing into the shape you want; 順德 lets it become what it would have been.

And 積小以高大: a measure, a step, a fraction — accumulated. The hexagram began with a scoop for grain, and it ends by saying what the scoop is for.

## The test

Take a rise you are in the middle of — a role, a reputation, a capability. Ask whether it is 升 (graduated, one grade at a time) or a jump. Then ask the last line's question: can you see where the next step lands? If not, the text's advice is not to stop climbing — it is to stop being depleted while climbing.
